title: Microhabitats
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Microhabitats Worksheets (Minibeasts Under Logs and Stones)
standard_code: Year 2: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited and describe how different habitats provide for the basic needs of different kinds of animals and plants. Identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats, including microhabitats.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on microhabitats: minibeasts under logs and stones, in leaf litter and soil, the woodlouse test and a minibeast hunt. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A microhabitat is a tiny habitat.
key_sub: Many minibeasts like dark, damp places such as under a log.
body_html:
How to think about it

A microhabitat is a very small habitat.

  • Under a log, in leaf litter or in the soil.
  • Many minibeasts like dark, damp places.
  • Look gently and put them back.
Example

Woodlice live where?

Dark and damp

Answer: under logs and stones

Example

A spider has how many legs?

Not an insect

Answer: eight

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a microhabitat is a tiny animal.
  • Thinking minibeasts like hot, dry places.
  • Thinking woodlice are insects.

faq.a: A very small habitat, such as the space under a log or a stone, a pile of leaves, or a crack in a wall.
Under a log it is dark, damp and cool, and there are rotting plants to eat. Woodlice dry out in hot, bright places.

faq.q: How do I go on a minibeast hunt?
faq.a: Gently lift logs and stones, look with a magnifying glass, record what you find, and put everything back carefully.
